message.content:
This appears to be from a CBP ruling on pallet blocks of particle board. Pallet components of wood are classified in 4415.20 (pallets, box pallets and other load boards; pallet collars), and parts of pallets fall under 4415.20.80 or 4415.20.40. Compressed wood blocks, though, could fall under 4421 (other articles of wood), or 4410 (particle board) if the block is merely cut pieces of particle board.

I recall the ruling on "molded wood pallet blocks": the blocks are made of wood particles agglomerated with resin, drilled, with eased corners. Because they are drilled and have eased corners, they are worked beyond simple cutting, so they would not stay in 4410 and would be classified as articles of wood. Pallet parts go to 4415.20 as "pallets... other load boards," which covers parts of pallets by the heading text "pallets, box pallets and other load boards." Parts of wood articles are generally classified with the articles, so 4415.20.80 is likely, though 4415.20.40 covers "pallets and other load boards" while 4415.20.80 is "other."

The 4415.20 subheadings are: 4415.20.20 pallets; 4415.20.40 box pallets and similar load boards; 4415.20.60 pallet collars; 4415.20.80 other. I am not certain of these, but I will go with 4415.20.8000. The alternative is 4421.99.98 for other articles of wood. Since the blocks are pallet components, I choose 4415.20.8000.

{"hts_code": "4415.20.8000", "reason": "Drilled, edge-eased particle board blocks are worked pallet components, so they are classified with pallets and load boards in heading 4415 rather than as plain particle board in 4410."}
